title: Burst coverage repricing and contract hiring sandbox — March 2026
content:
Purpose:
Quick sandbox for estimating the P&L and headcount impact of (A) an emergency burst-coverage repricing to preserve SLAs during a sustained demand spike and (B) a temporary contractor hiring plan to avoid capacity-driven price increases. This is intentionally rough — used for leadership tradeoff discussion.

Summary (1-paragraph):
We model three pricing levers (+15% surcharge on high-latency routes, temporary committed credits, and a short-lived spot reprice) and two hiring levers (convert backlog to contractors vs accelerate FTE hiring). Under a 4-week sustained 2x token demand spike, the fastest way to protect margins is a combination of a 10–15% short-term route surcharge and 8–12 additional contractor FTEs for serving-runtime + SRE. Aggressive FTE hiring delays runway ~3 months; contractors increase near-term OpEx but cap marginal cost.

Assumptions (key):
- Baseline monthly active token volume (pre-spike): 3.7B tokens
- Spike scenario: sustained 2.0x for 4 weeks then taper to 1.15x run-rate
- Unit cost (baseline): $0.0015 per 1k tokens (average across model mix after quantization savings)
- Reserved capacity amortized monthly: $420k (platform + infra leases)
- GPU spot variable cost increase during spike: +50% on variable portion if we rely on burst spots
- Average fully-burdened FTE cost: Eng $18k/mo, SRE $20k/mo, CS/Support $12k/mo, Sales $14k/mo
- Contractor blended rate (serving infra / runtime surge): $10k/mo equivalent per contractor (range $6–14k)
- Revenue: average price per 1k tokens (baseline customer mix): $2.25/1k tokens
- Elasticity: simple linear demand reaction to price with elasticity coefficients used below (conservative).

Scenario matrices (table-like rows). Numbers rounded. All monetary values USD/month unless called out.

SCENARIOS: baseline | spike-no-action | spike+pricing-surcharge | spike+contractors | spike+mixed

1) Volume (1k tokens): 3,700,000 | 7,400,000 | 7,400,000 | 7,400,000 | 7,400,000
2) Price per 1k tokens: $2.25 | $2.25 | $2.59 (+15%) | $2.25 | $2.40 (+6.7% blended)
3) Revenue: $8,325,000 | $16,650,000 | $19,166,000 | $16,650,000 | $17,760,000
4) Variable token cost baseline: $5,550 | $11,100 | $11,100 | $11,100 | $11,100  (in thousands: $5.55k -> actually scale to thousands; see notes)
   Note: For readability, line 4 values are shown as thousands (k) in the sheet. Actual variable cost = volume/1k * unit_cost.
5) Monthly OpEx add (contractors / surge infra / spot premium): $0 | $950k | $650k | $1,050k | $850k
6) Gross margin (approx):  >80% | ~50% | ~60% | ~45% | ~55%
7) Runway impact (months of cash until runway threshold): baseline unchanged | -1.8 months | -1.1 months | -2.0 months | -1.3 months

Interpretation notes on table:
- spike-no-action shows painful margin compression: doubled volume increases revenue but variable infra costs and spot premiums erode margin — runway shortens ~2 months in the model.
- spike+pricing-surcharge preserves margin best but risks demand drop; we modeled elasticity = -0.25 (conservative). With -0.25, surcharge reduces post-spike demand by ~8–10% (small), netting a ~5–7% revenue uplift vs no-action while protecting margin.
- spike+contractors reduces immediate capacity pressure but increases OpEx materially; contractors were modeled to be brought online in week 1 of the spike and de-provisioned after 6 weeks (pay for 2 months). This shows a deeper near-term cash hit but smoother SLA compliance.
- spike+mixed (6% blended surcharge + 6 contractor hires + limited reserved-burst credit) is our operationally-preferred compromise.

Headcount (hiring variables):
- Quick contractor pack: Eng-runtime contractors: 6; SRE contractors: 4; CS-support contractors: 2 => total 12 contractors. 
  - Onboarding assumptions: ramp to 50% capacity in 1 week, full capacity in 3 weeks.
  - Contingent cost: $10k/mo per contractor * 2 months = $240k net for the event (rounded to $250k in table).
- Rapid FTE hire alternative (slower): 8 FTEs split Eng(5)/SRE(2)/CS(1). Recruiting timeline 8–12 weeks; first full productivity in ~12 weeks. Costed as $18k–20k/month for average full burden + hiring overhead.

Microbreakdown: burst+mixed monthly delta (approx):
- Extra contractor OpEx: $120k (month 1) + $120k (month 2)
- Spot premium reduction due to surcharge: -$180k (we avoid some spot usage by shifting to reserved or throttling non-critical routes)
- Net monthly delta month 1: +$60k; month 2: -$60k (negative because surcharge revenue accrues against lower spot usage)

Customer & commercial considerations (qualitative):
- Surface the surcharge as a temporary SLA-preservation fee with explicit sunset and usage credit back if spike shortens <2 weeks. This reduces churn risk.
- For enterprise contracts, offer a short-term committed credit in exchange for priority support/guarantees (monetization + commercial stickiness).
- Communicate early to top 20 customers and provide usage dashboards; procurement/legal must approve credit language.

Open questions / risks:
- Elasticity uncertainty: if elasticity closer to -0.6 we risk larger churn; need to run customer cohorts (high-touch enterprise vs PLG) separately.
- Contractor onboarding risk (quality, security): need SRE-led ramp checklist; ensure background check / access gating for private deployments.
- Accounting for deferred revenue & credit issuance: finance tax/recognition implications for pre-paid credits.

Immediate recommended actions (next 72 hours):
1) Approve emergency surcharge playbook draft and prepare comms for top 20 accounts (owner: Luis) — target: 48h.
2) Prepare contractor sourcing list (vendor + internal bench) and author 2-week statement of work template (owner: Mira) — target: 72h.
3) Quantify elasticity by customer segment: export sample of top 50 customers usage over last three spikes (owner: Data Science) — target: 5 business days.
4) Draft legal-approved credit terms and support-level addendum (owner: Legal) — target: 5 days.

Appendix: quick calculation snippets (handy checks)
- Variable token cost quick check: volume(1k) * unit_cost = cost. Example: 7,400,000 * $0.0015 = $11,100 (k) => $11.1k.
- Surcharge revenue change (approx): baseline price * volume * surcharge_pct. e.g., 7.4M * ($2.25 * 15%) = ~$2.49M incremental in month of spike.

Action log (short):
- 2026-03-04: initial draft (Jordan)
- 2026-03-10: added contractor pack numbers (Mira)
- 2026-03-12: updated elasticity assumptions with DS (Ayesha)
- 2026-03-18: in-review with FP&A, awaiting legal language

Notes-to-self (rough):
- run cohort elasticity split: enterprise (0.0 to -0.15), mid-market (-0.2 to -0.5), PLG (-0.4 to -0.8).
- consider short-term feature gating instead of surcharge for PLG web tier (faster opt-in, lower comms).
- check dedicated pool size per region (apac vs na-eu) — regional spot exposure differs.

Finish.
